Reason: The chest X-ray shows a large, homogeneous opacity in the right mid-to-lower lung zone with preserved lung volume (no significant mediastinal shift), which, combined with the clinical history of a palpable posterior chest wall mass and decreased breath sounds, is most consistent with a chest wall tumor (such as lymphoma) extending into or compressing the lung parenchyma.
